findings.summary: The unchanged wgsl-fns smoothStep semantic workload calls getCompilationInfo through the public transparent observer. Pinned Dawn and Doe each return and record exactly one compilation-info result bound to the observed shader module, with no error diagnostics for the valid frozen shader.

Both providers share normalized shader, compilation-call, command, dispatch, synchronization, and mapped-readback identity ade1ea293c502e9746987e3e8963b3683e10e8bf4d1cc9fb1b7e83671125b00b. Each exact eight-float output has SHA-256 ad6a7f7fdc8f2f532d7a8ce04be449c1660e9f0776392427da25dca0c76c60b7.

limitations: The valid frozen shader produces no compiler messages, so this real-application gate proves getCompilationInfo call and module binding but not provider exposure of a non-empty diagnostic; package regression coverage separately records a normalized warning.
The observer records public JavaScript compilation information and commands, not native compiler stages, backend binaries, driver calls, or complete filesystem behavior.
The schema-required peak-memory fields are zero because this bounded admission runner did not collect a process high-water mark; zero is not a measured memory claim.
This result does not reopen the terminal wgsl-fns runtime-ownership decision and grants no performance, promotion, or release credit.
